messages:
Alex (Support): FYI ACME reported sudden 5xx spike + tail latency on their Dedicated pool eu2-dedicated-42 around 09:04 UTC. They see errors across multiple routes. Attaching summary from them below. :eyes:
Liam (Eng Runtime): can you paste the top-level errors? 5xx from API or internal timeouts?
Alex (Support): customer pasted this snippet:

```
2026-03-16T09:03:52Z ERROR gen: recv failed: rpc deadline exceeded
2026-03-16T09:03:54Z WARN model: token generation slowed, latency > 2s
2026-03-16T09:04:01Z ERROR runtime: 5xx internal: inference kernel busy
```

Alex (Support): They ran a simple repro load: 20 concurrent requests using our v1/generate endpoint, each with batch_size=16 using the customer model. Provided curl: 

```
for i in {1..20}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"acme/llm-prod","input":"test","batch_size":16}' &
done; wait
```

Alex (Support): They say errors started ~3m after steady load.
Sofia (Eng SRE): pinging node telemetry now. Which pool? eu2-dedicated-42, correct?
Alex (Support): yes.
deploy-bot: autoscaler: scale event: pool eu2-dedicated-42 at 09:05 UTC, attempted node add but capacity constrained, action=queue
Liam (Eng Runtime): interesting — autoscaler queued because no spare hosts in region. Could be that one tenant is saturating GPUs and blocking scheduling. Do we have per-tenant elect throttles active?
Sofia (Eng SRE): checking MIG slice telemetry. Early signs: one MIG slice shows sustained SM utilization ~98% and SM busy stalls high. Memory usage moderate. Suggests compute-bound saturation, not memory OOM.
Alex (Support): customer insists it was "noisy neighbor" because other tenants on same host saw latency too.
Liam (Eng Runtime): possible. Ask them to run the repro with smaller batch_size (1) to confirm it's batch amplification. Also need kernel-level traces. Can you request nvtx or our lightweight perf dump?
Alex (Support): sent repro suggestion. They ran batch_size=1 and errors dropped to 0, tail latency stable. They also shared this lightweight perf dump from our agent:

```
host: gpu-node-73
gpu0: sm_active_pct=97.4, sm_avg_occupancy=95, sm_warp_issue=high
kernel: matmul_v2 time=1.8ms x10000
```

Sofia (Eng SRE): that matmul kernel hot loop is classic for a model with large feeding dims + big batch. On MIG partitions, a heavy kernel can hog SMs affecting siblings.
Liam (Eng Runtime): confirm MIG config for that host: 1g.10gb? If the tenant is on a larger share than others, but still hogging SM due to big batch, we could see cross-slice interference. Also check L3 bandwidth counters.
Sofia (Eng SRE): I pulled host config: GPU has 7g.40gb MIG slices, multiple tenants on same physical GPU. L3 and SM stalls spiking. This is noisy neighbor.
Alex (Support): customer requests immediate mitigation — they want their capacity isolated. What are options short-term?
Liam (Eng Runtime): options:
- Migrate ACME to an empty node (preferred) if spare hosts available.
- Temporarily lower their max_concurrent_requests or enforce lower batch_size via route-level policy.
- Adjust autoscaler to prioritize adding nodes for Dedicated pool (but deploy-bot said region constrained).
- In medium-term, tune kernel scheduling and introduce per-tenant kernel GPU QoS gating (hard).
Sofia (Eng SRE): short-term I can evict lower-priority tenants from that host and move them, freeing a whole MIG slice to ACME. Need approvals for eviction.
oncall: @oncall assigned to this thread.
Alex (Support): ACME approved a live migration window. They prefer minimal downtime.
Liam (Eng Runtime): If we migrate, we should also set a temporary route policy to cap batch_size=4 and concurrency=8 for ACME while migration completes. That will avoid re-triggering saturation on the new host until we have autoscale capacity.
Sofia (Eng SRE): I'll start eviction plan. Plan: 1) mark host cordon, 2) drain tenants with lowest priority, 3) migrate ACME to freed MIG slice, 4) monitor SM util + latency for 15m.
Alex (Support): noted. I'll tell ACME: we'll cap batch_size and concurrency, attempt migration, and follow up in 20m. :white_check_mark:
Liam (Eng Runtime): also creating a short-term rule in the control plane to reject requests that set batch_size>8 for Dedicated pools until we push a config change. Will add telemetry hook to detect recurrence.
Sofia (Eng SRE): eviction started 09:12 UTC. Will post updates.
Alex (Support): thanks — please post results.
Sofia (Eng SRE): update 09:23 UTC: eviction completed, ACME migrated to freed MIG slice on gpu-node-81. Initial metrics: sm_active_pct dropped to 45% on host, latency reduced from 1.9s p95 to 280ms p95. No 5xx observed in last 5m. :tada:
Alex (Support): relaying to ACME. They asked for next steps to prevent recurrence.
Liam (Eng Runtime): Recommended actions for ACME:
- Reduce default batch_size in client to 4 (or dynamic batching with token-length caps).
- Use our dedicated reservation with single-tenant nodes if predictable peak workload.
- We will introduce per-tenant burst tokens + kernel QoS in coming weeks; file created: RUNTIME-5642.
Sofia (Eng SRE): Ops actions for us:
- Add a soft limit alert: when a single tenant > 70% SM for > 2m on shared host, auto-evict low-priority tenants or trigger immediate autoscale override.
- Review autoscaler queue policy for region-constrained cases.
Alex (Support): ACME satisfied with cleanup and mitigation. Closing thread after postmortem doc. Thanks all.
Liam (Eng Runtime): adding postmortem note and tagging as noisy-neighbor, short-term mitigation applied.
Sofia (Eng SRE): saved perf dumps and kernel traces to the incident bucket.
deploy-bot: deploy: config patch queued to control plane to enforce batch_size cap for Dedicated routes.
